_note: Portfolio projects. Entries with "client": true are real client sites: linked live, no sample ads, no made-up results. The rest are fictional concepts; the pages say so, and each has a demo site in marketing/work/<slug>/ and sample ads on its case page. "listed": false keeps a case page building (for pages that link to it) but leaves it off the grids.

projects.name: Kirby’s Home Improvement
projects.summary: A one-page site for a father-and-son home improvement team in Spartanburg, built so a homeowner can call or ask for a free estimate in seconds.
projects.challenge: A family business that has painted and repaired homes around Spartanburg since 1994, almost entirely by word of mouth. People who heard about them had nowhere to look them up, see what they do or ask for a price.
approach: The free estimate form and a call button sit right at the top, so the next step is never more than one tap away.
Every service people call them for, in plain words, plus the towns they cover, so homeowners know quickly whether it’s a fit.
Their own story up front: one family, two generations, and you talk to a Kirby, not a call center.
built: One-page site, mobile first
Free estimate form sent to their inbox
Tap-to-call header on phones
Services, how it works and service area
Business details for Google: hours, area and services
Site Stats for calls and estimate requests

quote.text: The website was set up quick and more than professional. Leads come straight to my phone and it’s never been easier to keep up with the quotes.

projects.name: Hearth & Grain
projects.summary: A one-page site that sells the morning: today’s bakes, order-ahead pickup and catering, with Meta and Google ads for the busy weekend rush.
projects.challenge: A small bakery that sells out by noon. Most customers find it on Google Maps or Instagram, but there’s no way to order ahead, and catering requests get lost in DMs.
approach: One page, ordered the way customers decide: what’s fresh today, when you’re open, how to order ahead.
A pickup order button and a catering form above the fold on phones.
Big, warm type and real prices, so it reads like the chalkboard menu inside the shop.
built: One-page site, mobile first
Today’s menu with prices
Order-ahead and catering forms
Hours, map and directions
Site Stats goals for calls, orders and catering

projects.name: Ridgeline Heating & Air
projects.summary: A five-page site built around one action, calling, with Google call campaigns that run hardest when it’s hottest.
projects.challenge: A family HVAC company competing with national brands on Google. When the AC breaks, people call the first trustworthy number they see, so every second on the site matters.
approach: A tap-to-call button that follows you down the page on phones, and same-day availability shown up top.
A section for each service so Google can match “AC repair” and “furnace install” searches.
Financing and service area answered before anyone has to ask.

projects.name: Pine Street Dental
projects.summary: A calm, ten-page practice site with online booking and a blog, plus a new-patient campaign on Meta and Google.
projects.challenge: A growing practice that needs a steady flow of new patients. Nervous patients want to know who they’ll see, what it costs and whether their insurance works, before they ever call.
approach: Soft colors and plain answers: insurance, costs and what a first visit is like, all one tap from the home page.
A new-patient offer and online booking on every page.
A blog the front desk can update, for the questions patients ask every week.

projects.name: Loom & Lantern
projects.summary: An online store for hand-poured candles and woven throws, launched with TikTok and Meta ads made for the feed.
projects.challenge: A maker selling at weekend markets who wants to sell online all year. The products are beautiful in person, so the store and the ads have to carry that feeling on a phone screen.
approach: Scent-first shopping: browse by mood, with notes, burn time and size on every product.
A free-shipping bar and bundles that raise the order value without discounts.
Short behind-the-pour videos for TikTok and Reels, retargeted to people who watched.

projects.name: Fernhollow Interactive
projects.summary: A studio site with room to grow: every game gets a home, every role shows its pay, and press can find what they need in one click.
projects.challenge: A seven-person studio with one game out and a bigger one coming. Their old site was a single page with a store link, so press, players and job seekers all landed in the same place and nobody found what they came for.
approach: A page per game that sends players to the right place: the store for the game that’s out, the new game’s own site for the one that isn’t.
News and devlogs they publish themselves, so updates don’t wait on a developer.
A careers page with pay ranges on every role, and a press page with logos and keys in one place.
built: Home, Games, Studio, News + posts, Careers, Press, Contact
News and devlog posts the studio edits itself
Careers with pay ranges and a hiring process
Press page with fact sheet, logos and key requests
Newsletter and Discord sign-ups tracked in Site Stats

projects.name: Lampwright
projects.summary: A game site built to turn interest into wishlists, playtest sign-ups and Discord members, with a press kit ready before anyone asks.
projects.challenge: An unreleased game with a store page, a trailer and a Discord, but nowhere that tied them together. Wishlists and playtest interest were scattered, and press had to email to get a screenshot.
approach: One clear action on every page, Wishlist, with the playtest and Discord close behind.
A media page with the trailer and a screenshot gallery that works on a phone.
A full press kit page, so writers and creators never have to wait on an email.
